submissions.findingTextShort: A four-trial systematic review found short-term BPH symptom and urinary-flow improvements with beta-sitosterol preparations.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A systematic review of four double-blind randomized trials totaling 519 men with symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia found that beta-sitosterol-containing preparations improved urinary symptom scores, peak urinary flow, and residual urine versus placebo over 4 to 26 weeks, while long-term effectiveness and complication prevention remained unknown.
submissions.populationContext: Men with symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia across four randomized trials
submissions.usageContext: Heterogeneous beta-sitosterol-containing phytosterol preparations for 4 to 26 weeks
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Preparations were not standardized and treatment durations were short; this evidence does not support cholesterol claims or long-term BPH complication prevention.

submissions.findingTextShort: The BPH systematic review found symptom and flow benefits but no reduction in prostate size.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Within the four-trial BPH systematic review, beta-sitosterol preparations improved selected urinary symptoms and flow measures but did not reduce prostate size, so prostate-support wording must not imply gland shrinkage or disease modification.
submissions.usageContext: Beta-sitosterol-containing preparations in short randomized trials
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Outcome-specific null finding; symptom relief and prostate-size effects are distinct propositions.

submissions.findingTextShort: A major positive BPH trial used a product labeled beta-sitosterol that was actually a phytosterol mixture.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled multicenter BPH trial in 200 patients administered 20 mg three times daily of a product described as beta-sitosterol but explicitly containing a mixture of phytosterols, so the clinical outcome cannot be treated as proof that isolated beta-sitosterol alone produced the effect.
submissions.populationContext: Two hundred men with symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia
submissions.usageContext: Phytosterol mixture containing beta-sitosterol, 20 mg three times daily for six months
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Preparation-identity boundary; mixture evidence can contextualize the beta-sitosterol owner but cannot be silently converted into isolated-compound efficacy.

submissions.findingTextShort: Beta-sitosterol BPH evidence needs formulation-standardized, long-duration replication.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: The BPH evidence base is limited by short duration and nonstandardized preparations, including nonglucosidic phytosterol mixtures and a beta-sitosterol glucoside preparation with different results; future evidence grading must preserve formulation identity and long-term clinical outcomes.
submissions.populationContext: Men studied for symptomatic benign prostatic hyperplasia
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Research-gap conclusion, not a claim that all preparations are equivalent or ineffective.
